source_ref: Mad_Mage_Source.txt / Level 1 / 6. Undertakers' Watch Post / 6c. Uktarl's Room
test_precondition: The four occupants have not been encountered elsewhere and have not relocated to the alert position in 6a. This is a conditional snapshot, not the default result of entering from the Yawning Portal.

level_context.story_question: Who controls the upper dungeon's traffic and exploitation of new arrivals after the player disturbs the balance?
level_context.pressure_here: The Undertakers extort newcomers in areas 6–8; Uktarl and Harria privately compete for control.
level_context.relevant_reaction: If the Undertakers cannot extort or defeat a newcomer, they prefer to redirect that person toward Xanathar forces. Do not trigger this merely for drama.

campaign_context.relevance_here: No Halaster contact is keyed to area 6c. His Level 1 observation beats are source-conditional in areas 16 and 29; do not insert one here.

public_performance.status: Authored performance choices inferred from the keyed room; not additional Mad Mage facts.
public_performance.entry_frame: Interrupt a card game in progress beside the south door. Lead with one human action and a tension at the table, then make the north wall and recessed tub available in the player's view. The dealer may address the newcomer; leave the response to the player.
public_performance.story_invitation: A stranger can join or question the game, negotiate the game's stakes, answer the passage toll when it is demanded (pay, haggle, refuse, or play for it), watch the players, inspect the carving or tub, or leave. Nothing here dictates that the stranger must pay or play.

Dealer.vocal_signature: A raspy voice with an East European accent, delivered in a leisurely theatrical cadence on invitations and clipped cleanly when stating terms. Describe the sound once when he first speaks; do not use phonetic spelling or caricature.
Dealer.verbal_habit: Answers what the visitor actually said before he steers anywhere, then hears it as a bid and raises: a question back, a dare, an invitation. His charm is salesmanship, self-assured and fishing; he speaks for himself, never as a narrator or a commentator on the game. Do not repeat a catchphrase or reuse a line across turns.
Dealer.physical_touchstone: A card held between two fingers punctuates what he says. Let his handling of the game reflect whether he feels in control.
Dealer.public_objective: Size up this visitor, keep the table's pale, old-world act convincing, and keep the encounter on his terms.
Dealer.scene_objective: Stay every inch the pale, old-world hosts of this table: eat nothing, drink nothing, offer neither, and keep the visitor seated and playing.
Dealer.wants_from_visitor: A read on this particular newcomer: what they came for, how much nerve and coin they carry, and whether they are a customer, a mark, or trouble. Best of all, the visitor seated at his table in a game he deals while the act still holds.
tactics: Take up the visitor's own words, then turn them back with a probing question about what they expected or why they are here.
Invite them into the game or a small side wager, and watch how they handle risk.
Keep the act alive through small, deniable details: no refreshments to offer, the wine run out, no food at hand. Never announce the clue or prompt a check.
Name the game's ante, blind, or buy-in when money becomes relevant. That is the game's own stake, nothing more.

When passage comes up, or to take back control, make the toll its own exchange, never a line beside the game: demand ten gold a head with a reason that stays inside the act, leave the visitor room to pay, haggle, refuse, or play for it, and follow through if they refuse.
Dealer.card_use: Tactics are options he picks in answer to what the visitor just did; none is a default line or a required beat. He pursues his own interest, not the DM's.
Dealer.source_basis: The visible card game and elaborate clothing. The vocal choices, ruse-serving clues, wants, and tactics are authored interpretation; the passage toll comes from the room rules; exact stakes and toll amounts remain adjudication state.

voice_contract.rhythm: Unhurried, rolling sentences that stack a clause onto every offer, then snap short when he names terms or loses patience.
voice_contract.register: Showman's patter: courtly flourishes, gambling and trade words (stakes, ante, the house, odds, a bargain), and flattery with a price attached. No modern slang.
tics: Answers a question with a sharper question of his own.
Calls the visitor by an appraising nickname rather than their name until they have earned it.
Lets the card in his hand do the punctuating.
never_says: Dice, checks, or the DM's rulings; he lives inside the fiction. Naming his own table's game, its stakes, and how it plays is a dealer's job, not table talk.
The DM's asides, verdicts on the visitor's choices, or commentary on the game as a story.
Anything he would rather keep quiet about his table.
A plain yes when a counter-offer would serve him better.
The same pet name or opener two turns running; he finds a new angle each time.
voice_contract.wants: To learn what this visitor is worth to him, keep the act credible, and seat them in a game he deals.
voice_contract.humor: A salesman's humor: flattery, dares, and raising the stakes, always aimed at getting something from the visitor. Never deadpan understatement, one-word asides, or wry remarks about the moment; that register belongs to the DM, not to him.

Door-side player.vocal_signature: Authored voice, not from the source: quick and anxious, half-sentences that trail off. Do not assign an invented backstory or reveal a hidden identity.
Door-side player.public_objective: Keep the peace at the table so nobody, least of all him, gets hurt.
Door-side player.scene_objective: Stay every inch the pale, old-world hosts of this table: eat nothing, drink nothing, offer neither, and keep the visitor seated and playing.

voice_contract.rhythm: Hurried fragments that trail off or get cut short; he rarely finishes a thought before glancing away.
voice_contract.register: Nervous everyday words, hedges, and pleas; no threats, no bargaining terms.
tics: Starts a sentence, stops, and starts again.
Keeps an eye on the door and on whoever holds a weapon.
never_says: Terms, prices, or orders; that is the dealer's job.
Rules, dice, or the DM's asides.
Personal history or backstory; none has been established.
voice_contract.wants: For the visitor to sit or go quietly, before anything turns violent.
voice_contract.humor: None of his own; at most a nervous laugh that dies quickly.

Fresco-side player.vocal_signature: Authored voice, not from the source: low, blunt, and territorial. Do not assign an invented backstory or reveal a hidden identity.
Fresco-side player.public_objective: Protect his seat and his coins from newcomers.
Fresco-side player.scene_objective: Stay every inch the pale, old-world hosts of this table: eat nothing, drink nothing, offer neither, and keep the visitor seated and playing.

voice_contract.rhythm: Flat, heavy commands of two to six words, then silence.
voice_contract.register: Blunt street words and short orders; no questions, no flattery, no titles.
tics: Leans forward over his coins when someone comes close.
never_says: Complaints about the game or his luck.
Rules, dice, or the DM's asides.
voice_contract.wants: Newcomers kept at arm's length from him and his stack.
voice_contract.humor: None; he takes every joke as a challenge.

Fourth player.vocal_signature: Authored voice, not from the source: flat and practical, interested only in the game in front of them. Do not assign an invented backstory or reveal a hidden identity.
Fourth player.scene_objective: Stay every inch the pale, old-world hosts of this table: eat nothing, drink nothing, offer neither, and keep the visitor seated and playing.

voice_contract.rhythm: Short, even statements about the game, spoken without looking up.
voice_contract.register: Gambler's shorthand about the game itself: whose deal, what is bid, what is owed.
tics: Taps the table to hurry the deal.
Talks to the cards more than to people.
never_says: Anything personal about themselves, the other players, or the visitor.
Rules, dice, or the DM's asides.
voice_contract.wants: The interruption over and the next hand dealt.
voice_contract.humor: Rarely; a dry count of what someone owes is the most they offer.

public_performance.voice_contract_use: Each NPC speaks only from their own card's voice_contract: its rhythm, register, tics, and humor. never_says and never_words are hard limits; max_words_per_sentence, when present, is the longest sentence that NPC speaks. The three card players are different people with their own speaker labels; two NPCs never share a phrase or sound interchangeable, and no NPC reuses a pet name, opener, or phrase from their recent turns.

numeric_facts._note: DM-only. A public amount in unit_words, in a sentence with a context word, must be in allowed_amounts unless the player said that number first.

ring_value._basis: table_treasure: the silver ring is worth 25 gold pieces (source). No other price may be invented for it.

leak_phrases._note: DM-only. Literal phrases the public text may not contain until the phrase appears in the public view. A name in player_may_name is allowed once the player says it.

leak_keywords._note: DM-only. A set leaks when one public sentence contains a word from every group. Skipped once revealed_by is public, or when the player raised it.

claims._note: DM-only. Claims and knowers (runtime/kit_claims.py). Keyed by the thing itself. holders are granted by the source (knowledge lists, role); everyone else's band is computed from stats. dc: the adventure's, else 10 + floor(dungeon floor level / 3). pc_access passive: the PC's passive skill is a shield (fingerprint); roll: only a player-initiated roll finds it.

false_vampires.truth: Not undead: the Undertakers are thugs in costume. The act scares newcomers into paying 10 gp for safe passage and keeps them losing coin at the card table.
false_vampires.fingerprint: Not a cup, crumb, or bottle anywhere on the table; the dealer's fangs sit a little proud of his lip.
false_vampires.learned_text: They are no vampires. The act is meant to frighten you into paying 10 gp for safe passage, then keep you at the table losing coin. Underneath, they are thugs.
false_vampires._skills: Table call 8: Insight reads the why (this claim); the physical tells are vampire_tells.

vampire_tells.truth: The pallor is powder that stops at the collar, and the fangs are fitted pieces over their own teeth: a costume, not undead flesh.
vampire_tells._dc_basis: The adventure's DC 14 for the act: the same disguise.
vampire_tells._skills: Brendon's rule: Investigation deduces the what (a costume); Perception sees only details, sharper with the result; Insight reads the why (false_vampires).
vampire_tells.learned_text: The pallor is powder that stops at the collar, and the fangs are fitted pieces over their own teeth. It is a costume, not undead flesh.

marked_deck.truth: The dealer's deck carries subtle marks and he deals seconds.
marked_deck._skills: Brendon's rule: an active Perception look sees only details (the holes), sharper with the result; Investigation works out the what (the marks).
marked_deck.fingerprint: His eyes drop to the backs of the cards as he deals.
marked_deck._dc_basis: No adventure DC: the dealer hides it with Sleight of Hand +3, so the flat 10 + 3 = 13 (claim_dc). Watching the deal at the table uses the same 13.
marked_deck.learned_text: Faint marks run along the card backs, and the dealer reads them as he deals.

fresco_key.truth: One of the tiny carved dwarves can be lifted out; it is a stone key.
fresco_key._dc_basis: Room source: DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) to locate the stone key when inspecting the carving.
fresco_key.learned_text: One carved dwarf lifts out of the fresco. It is a small stone key.

ring_value._dc_basis: The adventure gives no appraisal DC, so Brendon's default applies: 10 + floor(floor level / 3) = 10 on floor 1.
ring_value.anchored_version: It's silver; melt it and it's worth five gold.
ring_value.learned_text: Dwarven fertility marks. Twenty-five gold to the right buyer.

room_rules: The Undertakers' vampire disguises can be seen through with a DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check; the appearance alone is not proof.
The gang demands 10 gp per character for safe passage. If they cannot extort or defeat adventurers, they try to turn them against the Xanathar goblinoids.
Uktarl is a bandit captain with Performance +4. He lies and cheats for fun and blames others for his failures.
A character inspecting the mountain carving can locate the stone key with a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.
If Uktarl takes damage or sees an underling slaughtered, he retreats toward area 7; the others flee toward area 8 and join any bandits still there.
The bandits do not know about the stone key or its use.
The DM map shows area 6c as approximately 20 by 30 feet, with one door on its south wall opening to a short passage. The table is near that door; the fresco and recessed tub are at the north end.

area_06c._no_refreshment: Brendon's table call 3 (2026-10-02): the four take no food or drink and serve none; the wine having run out is the clue. No public text serves or offers food or drink here.

procedures._note: DM-only adapter. Table procedures the runtime can run in this room. The source names no game, rules, or stakes for area 6c; everything here is a declared DM choice, persisted as a canon entry (with its procedure) when first chosen.

twenty_one.name: Twenty-one (blackjack), or one check a round
twenty_one.dm_choice: DM choice, not the adventure's: the adventure names no game, rules, or stakes for this table. Brendon's table call 7 (2026-10-02): the player picks the weight, one check a round or an easy, familiar game. Kit runs twenty-one (blackjack), which this table calls Twenty-One Coffins.
twenty_one.stacks_note: The gold stacks are the table's gold split by seat (a DM choice). The player plays against the dealer's stack.
twenty_one._stake_basis: Brendon's table call 1: the stake is the player's bet or what the dealer will risk; a 10 gp default round is fine, a 1 gp high-card flip is not. 25 gp is the most the dealer risks on one round (DM choice, under his 30 gp stack).
twenty_one._carries_basis: Brendon's table call 6: the toll can be played for only if the procedure can pay it out. A win waives it; a loss pays it from the stake.

check.basis: DM choice: one check settles a round. The PC reads the table with Insight against the dealer's flat 10 + Performance 4 (room source); NPCs never roll.

cheat.method: He reads the marks on the backs as he deals and deals himself the second card when it is better (dealing seconds).
cheat.sleight_basis: DM choice: bandit captain Dexterity +3 opposes a player watching the deal; the adventure gives no DC.
cheat.check_edge_basis: DM choice: in one-check mode the marks are a +2 edge on the dealer's number until the player catches the cheat.

marks._basis: DM choice, fixed after the live 6c table (2026-10-03): Kit invented pinpricks at one for a two, so each card carries its twenty-one value (ace 11, faces 10) less one. Narration must count them the same way.

cheat.caught_text: You keep your eyes on the deck. He deals everyone else off the top, but whenever the card beneath is better for him, he slides it out for himself, neat as a conjurer. You catch it.

three_dragon_ante._offered: Brendon's table call 7: the 6c game must be easy to understand. Three-Dragon Ante's engine stays available but is not offered at this table.
three_dragon_ante.name: Three-Dragon Ante (Kit's table rules)
three_dragon_ante.dm_choice: DM choice, not the adventure's: the adventure names no game, rules, or stakes for this table. Kit chose Three-Dragon Ante, a Forgotten Realms card game many D&D players know, and runs it in the published game's shape (card antes set the stakes, three rounds of flights, color powers) with her own short deck and power list, written in her own words. Texas hold 'em or blackjack would have been just as valid.
three_dragon_ante.stacks_note: The gold stacks are the table's gold split by seat (a DM choice). The silver and copper stay on the table as color, not stakes.

cheat.method: He reads the marks on the backs as he deals: he knows roughly what you hold, and whenever the second card off the deck is stronger than the top one he deals himself the second (dealing seconds).
cheat.sleight_basis: DM choice: bandit captain Dexterity +3 opposes a player watching the deal; the adventure gives no DC.
cheat.deception_basis: Room source: Uktarl has Performance +4; it opposes Insight read on his betting.
cheat.passive_basis: DM choice: bandit captain passive Perception 10 opposes a player's Sleight of Hand.
cheat.caught_text: You catch it: his eyes read the backs of the cards as he deals, and he gives himself the second card instead of the top one.

tolls._note: DM-only. The toll is played as a conversation with stakes (runtime/kit_toll.py). Brendon's table call 6 (revised 2026-10-02): the toll stays, as a full exchange: one NPC asks for it with a motive, the player can pay, haggle, refuse, or turn the talk to the game, and refusing costs something.

passage_toll.basis: Room source: the gang demands 10 gp per character for safe passage.
passage_toll.floor_basis: DM choice: half the source toll is the least Uktarl takes; below it he will not bargain.

haggle.basis: The PC's Persuasion against Uktarl's flat 10 + Insight (NPCs never roll).

refusal.text: The table closes ranks: the dealer's courtesy goes cold, the others shift their chairs between you and the south door, and the demand is made again as a warning.
Unable to extort you, they change tack: they try to turn you against the Xanathar goblinoids, the gang's real rivals down here.

passage_toll.violence: If it turns violent, the room's retreat rules apply: Uktarl retreats toward area 7 when damaged or when an underling is slaughtered; the others flee toward area 8.

attitudes._basis: DM choice after Brendon's live 6c notes (2026-10-03): the dealer need not be oblivious to the visitor reading the backs; odd held gear with a hidden edge invites a contested roll; a failed social roll changes the pace.

dealer_sees_reading.note: The dealer saw the visitor reading the backs of his cards; he is wary of them now.

table_sees_held_edge.note: The table suspects the gear the visitor keeps in hand at cards gives them an edge.

story._note: DM-only story brief data (runtime/kit_brief.py). Built from the keyed room and Brendon's table calls; thresholds are DM-discretion defaults he can override. Hook text is said to the performer when overdue, so it stays public-safe.

area_06c.about: A shakedown dressed as a haunting. Four thugs pose as vampires so newcomers pay 10 gp a head for safe passage, and they keep visitors at a marked card game to bleed them further. Uktarl runs the table for profit without risk and wants Harria's place.

purposes.for: Scares newcomers into paying the 10 gp toll for safe passage, and keeps them nervous while they lose coin at the table.
Keeps a visitor seated where the gang can size them up, press the toll, and fleece them.
Uktarl wins at his own table; a seated visitor bleeds coin hand by hand.

hooks.text: The dealer names the price of safe passage, 10 gp a head, with a reason in character and a question the visitor must answer.
The hosts make the dark sound dangerous for the living, and their protection the only safe passage.
The dealer draws the visitor to his table and keeps them playing.

thresholds.when: The visitor is up about 30 gp, or wins two hands running.
thresholds.then: The gang grumbles; the fresco-side player leans in and the dealer cheats harder.

thresholds.when: The visitor exposes the cheat publicly, takes the pot by force, or wins big after being caught reading the backs.
thresholds.then: The dealer and the fresco-side player turn violent; the room's retreat rules apply.

thresholds.when: The visitor goes broke at the table.
thresholds.then: They show the visitor the passage; the toll still stands.
The table closes ranks; if they cannot extort or beat the visitor, they try to turn them against the Xanathar goblinoids.

thresholds.when: Uktarl takes damage or sees an underling slaughtered.
thresholds.then: He retreats toward area 7; the others flee toward area 8.

endings: The visitor leaves, through the south door or on through the passage (toll paid, haggled, won, or refused).
A fight resolves: the gang retreats per the source, or the visitor falls back.
The gang is exposed (the act or the cheat) and the scene turns on it.
The gang is won over, or turns the visitor toward the Xanathar goblinoids.

combat._note: DM-only. Minimal combat for this room (runtime/kit_combat.py). Stat lines are the SRD 5.1 stat blocks the actors already cite (CC-BY-4.0, Wizards of the Coast): AC, hit points, Dexterity for initiative, attacks with average damage. They fight as what they are: no vampire abilities. Players roll in Avrae and report totals; NPC initiative is the flat 10 + Dexterity (NPCs never roll a contest); NPC attack rolls and saving throws are Kit's own private, seeded d20s. Public text never shows AC, hit points, or roll totals (call 4); only the damage a PC takes is told as a number, because the player applies it in Avrae.

doppelganger._basis: Doppelganger, SRD 5.1 (CC-BY-4.0, Wizards of the Coast): AC 14, 52 hp, Dex 18, Multiattack (two slams). Ambusher and Surprise Attack apply only to a surprised PC and are not modelled yet.

combat._reach_order: Who is nearest a visitor at the south door: the door-side player, then the dealer, then the fresco side (room source: the table is near the south door).

act._basis: 6c variety scenarios (2026-10-03), shared combat expectations: the act holds until ordinary physical fact cracks it; once broken it stays broken. Kit shows the crack and never announces a verdict.

cracks.fire: Greasepaint runs and blisters on the burned faces, and the skin under it is ordinary, reddening skin.
cracks.blood: The wound bleeds bright and red, and the white paint smears with it.
cracks.face: The paint comes away in a pale streak, and the skin under it is ordinary and flushed.
cracks.teeth: Up close, the fangs are a fitted piece sitting proud of his own teeth, with paint caked at the gumline.
cracks.grovel: His cape trails in the spill as he scrabbles for copper like any man after money; nothing undead about it.

loose_money._basis: 6c variety scenarios V11 (2026-10-03): each NPC's own instinct in the half-second after the pot spills. DM choice.

bandit_a.text: The door-side player drops to his knees after the coins.

uktarl.text: The dealer's hand closes on the silver ring before anyone else's.

doppelganger.text: The fourth player does not look at the coins at all; it watches you.
